question.text: In bromination of Propyne, with Bromine <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn></math>-tetrabromopropane is obtained in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>27</mn><mo>%</mo></math> yield. The amount of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn></math> tetrabromopropane obtained from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of Bromine in this reaction is_____<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> . (Molar Mass : Bromine <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mn>80</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>mol</mi></math>)

solution.text:
According to the above chemical reaction, 2 moles of bromine will give one mole of the product.

2 moles of Br2 = 2×160 g of Br2 gives one mole of product = 360 g of product

So, mass of product formed from 1 gm of Br2 will be =3602×160 ×1g = 98 g of product

But given that % yield = 27%.

So actual amount of product = 98×27100 = 0.30 gram

=3.0×10-1 g
